finding.claim: validate uses !== with || so each condition is always true and valid payloads always report errors.
finding.title: validate condition always true

verifier.reason: The conditions at src/validation.ts:8 and src/validation.ts:11 use !== undefined || !== null, which is tautologically true for any value, so both errors are always pushed even for valid payloads.

finding.claim: buildSummary pushes into module-level totals then summarizes totals, so repeated calls double-count prior entries.
finding.title: ledger summary accumulates across calls

verifier.reason: buildSummary at src/ledger.ts:12-15 calls post(entries), which pushes into the module-level totals at src/ledger.ts:6-9, then iterates all of totals with no reset inside buildSummary, so a second call re-summarizes entries from the first call.

finding.claim: rotateToken does not await store.save before store.get, so the read can race the write.
finding.title: rotateToken missing await on save

verifier.reason: At src/session.ts:2 save returns Promise<void>, but src/session.ts:11 calls store.save without await before src/session.ts:12 returns store.get(userId), so the read can race the unfinished write.

finding.claim: collect uses forEach with async callback and returns immediately, so results is returned before tasks complete.
finding.title: collect does not await tasks

verifier.reason: Confirmed: src/analytics.ts:6 uses tasks.forEach with an async callback whose returned promises are discarded, and src/analytics.ts:12 returns results synchronously without awaiting them, so the array is returned before awaited task pushes at src/analytics.ts:7 complete.

finding.claim: start overwrites this.timer with a new setInterval without clearing an existing interval, leaking the prior timer.
finding.title: Scheduler start replaces timer without clear

verifier.reason: Confirmed at src/scheduler.ts:7-11: start() directly assigns this.timer = setInterval(...) with no prior clearInterval or running guard, and no stop/clear method exists in src/scheduler.ts:13-20, so a second call orphans the previous interval.

finding.claim: sort without comparator sorts lexicographically, so numeric scores order incorrectly and topScore can be wrong.
finding.title: numeric sort uses default lexicographic order

verifier.reason: The code at src/scores.ts:2 calls scores.slice().sort() with no comparator, which sorts numbers lexicographically as strings in JavaScript, and topScore at src/scores.ts:7 returns the last sorted element, so the maximum can be incorrect.

finding.claim: pageSlice uses slice(start, end + 1) where end is already start+size, returning size+1 items instead of one page.
finding.title: pageSlice off-by-one returns extra item

verifier.reason: Confirmed: at src/paging.ts:9 end is already start+size (exclusive bound for slice), so src/paging.ts:10 slice(start, end + 1) returns size+1 items when available.

finding.claim: withinQuota uses < while documented max is inclusive, so used+amount exactly equal to max is wrongly rejected.
finding.title: withinQuota excludes inclusive max

verifier.reason: At src/quota.ts:2-3 max is documented as inclusive, but src/quota.ts:6 uses strict <, so used+amount == max returns false.

finding.claim: normalizeSettings uses || so explicit 0 is replaced by defaults, while 0 is documented as legitimate.
finding.title: normalizeSettings treats 0 as missing

verifier.reason: normalizeSettings at src/settings.ts:13-14 uses || so an explicit 0 is replaced by 20/1000, contradicting src/settings.ts:18 stating 0 is a legitimate settings value and the null-only fallback pattern at src/settings.ts:20.
